Rainbow Runner

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A middle-aged man who had never run more than a marathon before, has broken the 25 year-old world record for the fastest journey on foot from Cape to Cairo

Unique Selling Point:
Keith Boyd is 57 years old and has a congenital heart condition. But he has just become the record holder for the fastest time on foot between Cape Town and Cairo. Averaging more than a marathon per day since July 2023, enduring injury, danger, and bureaucratic delays, Keith completed the 11 000km journey last week...all in an effort to motivate Africa's young people to vote for better leadership and a brighter future on the continent.

Summary:
Keith Boyd, the founder of Rainbow Leaders and the "Rainbow Runner" is a family man, entrepreneur, and extreme adventurer who embarked on a monumental quest to break the 25-year-old Guinness Book of Records for the Fastest journey from Cape Town to Cairo on foot, leaving on 27 July 2023, at 11:00 AM from the iconic V&A Waterfront.

Facts - ran 10793,1km in total. Departed Cape Town, 27 July 2023 and arrived on 21 April 2024 in Cairo on day 270. Returned to Ethiopia and ran 568,4km to complete the run on 22 May 2024 on Day 301 at Metema.

Crossed 9 countries: South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, Egypt, Return to Ethiopia

Country / Dates / Days / Distance
South Africa / 27 July - 11 Sept / Day 1-47 / 1857,7 km
Botswana / 11 Sept - 25 Sept / Day 47 – 61 / 653,6km
Zimbabwe / 25 Sept – 29 Sept / Day 61- 64 / 104,9km
Zambia / 29 Sept – 31 Oct / Day 61-97 / 1464,7km
Tanzania / 31 Oct – 25 Nov / Day 97 – 121 / 1179,6km
Kenya / 25 Nov – 16 Dec / Day 121 – Day 143 ( 1 day no running) / 928,1km
Ethiopia / 16 Dec – 14 Feb / Day 143 – Day 203 ( 27 days no running) / 1109,6km [logistical challenges]
Sudan / 14 Feb – 27 March / Day 203 – Day 245 (5 days no running – 4 ill) / 1719,8km
Egypt / 27 March – 21 April / Day 245 – Day 270 (finish at Cairo Tower) /1206,7km
Egypt / 22 April – 25 April / Day 271 – 274
Return to Ethiopia 25 April Day 274, started running 11 May on Day 290 to Day 301 on 22 May (19 days no running) / 568,4km

Further information:
Rainbow Leaders is an African NPO dedicated to enhancing youth engagement in the democratic process. Through various educational programs and initiatives, they aim to empower young people to become informed, active voters, leading to positive change in their communities and the nation. The Rainbow Run aims to raise awareness and, subsequently, encourage sponsorship and donations to support Rainbow Leaders in their mission to visit more high schools and inspire scholars about the significance of voter registration.

The previous record was held by Nicholas Bourne (UK) who ran from Cape Town, South Africa, to Cairo, Egypt, in 318 days from 21 January to 5 December 1998, covering over 12,069 km (7,500 miles) and passing through Botswana, Zambia, Tanzania, Kenya, Ethiopia, and Sudan. Bourne, a former international catwalk model went through 30 pairs of trainers; covered more than 67 km (42 miles) a day; reached altitudes of 3,657 m (12,000 ft); came face to face with a giant cobra, lions and herds of elephants; and raised one million pounds for the Born Free Foundation and Save The Children.

Keith was one of three runners moving from South to North in Africa at the same time - and he was by far the oldest competitor in an epic footrace. A British runner was aiming to cover the full length of Africa from Cape Agulhas to Morocco. The third runner, Ugandan-born, was running from Cape Town to London. Keith led the charge with the highest daily average run of over a marathon distance, 42.2 km, per day.
